title: Quantum Horizon and Quantum Membrane Paradigm from Black Hole Quantum Mechanics
abstract: We develop a microscopic quantum membrane paradigm from the matrix quantum mechanics of black holes [1]. It was proposed that a quantum black hole is described by a fuzzy sphere together with a half-filled Fermi sea of horizon partons. We show that the topology of the fuzzy sphere induces a Berry monopole, providing a microscopic origin for the monopole appearing in the tunneling description of the decay of quantum black hole. Because the partons couple to the fuzzy sphere as fundamental degrees of freedom, they are sensitive to this monopole and form Lowest-Landau-Level (LLL) states rather than ordinary propagating two-dimensional fermions. Their guiding-center dynamics generates Ohmic, Hall, and polarization currents on the horizon. To couple these currents to an external electromagnetic field, we introduce a two-block matrix configuration comprising black-hole, environmental, and bifundamental link sectors. Off-diagonal link modes become tachyonic near the fuzzy sphere and condense, dynamically locking the horizon gauge field to the boundary value of the external Maxwell field. The parton current thereby becomes a physical boundary source for the exterior field. Our construction replaces the fictitious membrane of the classical paradigm with a dynamical quantum membrane populated by microscopic LLL degrees of freedom. The resulting boundary condition generalizes the classical ingoing membrane condition and yields explicit quantum, frequency-dependent, and helicity-dependent corrections, offering a possible probe of the microscopic quantum structure of the horizon.
summary: This paper constructs a 'quantum membrane paradigm' for black hole horizons by modeling them using matrix quantum mechanics. It shows that the horizon dynamics are governed by Lowest-Landau-Level (LLL) states on a fuzzy sphere, which generate measurable electric currents. This microscopic description provides a physical origin for boundary conditions previously treated classically.
main_problem: To develop a microscopic quantum membrane paradigm for black hole horizons by providing a physical origin for boundary conditions typically used in classical descriptions.
main_result: The construction replaces the fictitious classical membrane with a dynamical quantum membrane populated by LLL degrees of freedom, yielding explicit quantum corrections to horizon boundary conditions.
method: The authors use matrix quantum mechanics models involving fuzzy spheres and Fermi seas to derive effective field theories for the horizon dynamics.
model_or_system: The system models quantum black holes using a matrix quantum mechanics framework equivalent to a fuzzy sphere coupled with a half-filled sea of 'horizon partons.'
key_observables: Ohmic, Hall, and polarization currents on the horizon; generalized boundary conditions for external electromagnetic fields.
important_parameters: The rank $N$ of the matrix model ($N=2J+1$) determines the monopole charge $c_1 = N-1$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the system to a matrix quantum mechanics description and utilizing large-$N$ limits.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the fuzzy sphere/Fermi sea structure, deriving the Berry monopole, analyzing LLL dynamics leading to transport currents, and finally introducing link variables whose condensation locks the horizon gauge field to external fields.
why_interesting: While focused on gravity, the use of LLL states, topological structures (Berry monopole), and emergent current generation from fundamental degrees of freedom shares conceptual overlap with strongly correlated electron systems and quantum Hall physics.
